views.name: hcpcs_canonical
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  HCPC AS hcpcs_code,
  SAFE_CAST(RECID AS INT64) AS recid,
  SEQNUM AS seqnum,
  LONG_DESCRIPTION AS long_description,
  SHORT_DESCRIPTION AS short_description,
  PRICE1 AS price1_raw,
  PRICE2 AS price2_raw,
  PRICE3 AS price3_raw,
  PRICE4 AS price4_raw,
  SAFE_CAST(MCM1 AS FLOAT64) AS mcm1,
  SAFE_CAST(MCM2 AS INT64) AS mcm2,
  STATUTE AS statute,
  COV AS coverage_indicator,
  ASC_GRP AS asc_group,
  ADD_DT AS add_date,
  ACT_EFF_DT AS active_effective_date,
  TERM_DT AS termination_date,
  ACTION_CD AS action_active_flag
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.hcpcs`
grain: hcpcs_code, recid  -- one row per HCPCS code version (RECID)

params.description: Canonical reference of HCPCS procedure/service codes and their attributes (one row per HCPCS code version RECID). Answers what a given HCPCS code means, its descriptions, effective/termination dates, pricing fields and basic classification flags.
params.when_to_use: Lookup metadata for a specific HCPCS code (descriptions, add/active/termination dates, statute, coverage indicator). | Filter or join by HCPCS code and RECID when analyzing claims or utilization that reference a specific HCPCS RECID/version. | Compose pricing or classification summaries (use price1..price4_raw, mcm1/mcm2, asc_group) when building measures by HCPCS code. | Determine code lifecycle (add_date, active_effective_date, termination_date) for time-aware joins to event/claims data.
params.output_schema: hcpcs_code: HCPC code string (derived from table field HCPC). | recid: RECID for the specific HCPCS code version, cast to INT64 (derived from RECID). | seqnum: sequence number/version indicator (derived from SEQNUM). | long_description: long textual description of the HCPCS code (derived from LONG_DESCRIPTION). | short_description: short textual description (derived from SHORT_DESCRIPTION). | price1_raw: raw numeric value from PRICE1 (derived from PRICE1). | price2_raw: raw numeric value from PRICE2 (derived from PRICE2). | price3_raw: raw numeric value from PRICE3 (derived from PRICE3). | price4_raw: raw numeric value from PRICE4 (derived from PRICE4). | mcm1: numeric/multiplier field MCM1 cast to FLOAT64 (derived from MCM1). | mcm2: numeric/multiplier field MCM2 cast to INT64 (derived from MCM2). | statute: statute/classification text (derived from STATUTE). | coverage_indicator: coverage indicator flag (derived from COV). | asc_group: ambulatory surgery center group classification (derived from ASC_GRP). | add_date: date the code was added (derived from ADD_DT). | active_effective_date: date the code became active (derived from ACT_EFF_DT). | termination_date: date the code was terminated (derived from TERM_DT). | action_active_flag: action code indicating active/inactive status (derived from ACTION_CD).
params.metric: hcpcs_code = HCPC (identity string column) | recid = SAFE_CAST(RECID AS INT64) (RECID cast to integer) | mcm1 = SAFE_CAST(MCM1 AS FLOAT64) (MCM1 cast to float) | mcm2 = SAFE_CAST(MCM2 AS INT64) (MCM2 cast to integer) | price1_raw = PRICE1 (raw price field, no aggregation applied) | price2_raw = PRICE2 (raw price field, no aggregation applied) | price3_raw = PRICE3 (raw price field, no aggregation applied) | price4_raw = PRICE4 (raw price field, no aggregation applied)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact/usage tables on hcpcs_code and/or recid — safe when the fact table is the many side (claims/events) because hcpcs_canonical is one-row-per (hcpcs_code, recid) and will not duplicate its own rows. Example: JOIN claims_table ON claims_table.hcpcs_code = hcpcs_canonical.hcpcs_code (or on recid if claims reference RECID). | You can join to dimensional tables that are one-row-per-hcpcs_code (if present) on hcpcs_code safely because both sides are one-row-per-code. | Do NOT join hcpcs_canonical to other tables/views that are one-to-many with respect to (hcpcs_code, recid) without first aggregating the many-side back to the (hcpcs_code, recid) grain. Joining directly to a one-to-many table (for example, a hypothetical hcpcs_tag_assignments table that stores multiple tags per RECID) will multiply rows and therefore multiply any measures derived from this view if you treat them as measures. Re-aggregate the many-side (e.g., ARRAY_AGG or GROUP BY recid/hcpcs_code) before joining if you need to preserve measure counts. | Do NOT assume price*_raw or mcm* are aggregates — they are raw attributes at the view grain. If you need totals (sum of price across codes) compute aggregates in a query grouping by the expected grain; do not rely on joins to one-to-many tables to produce correct sums without aggregation. | When composing time-aware filters (e.g., join to events by event_date), use active_effective_date and termination_date to restrict which RECID/version applies at the event date (e.g., WHERE event_date BETWEEN active_effective_date AND COALESCE(termination_date, '9999-12-31')). This prevents accidental duplication from matching multiple RECID rows for the same code-version period.

views.description: Canonicalized HCPCS code dimension: one row per HCPC+RECID with cleaned, consistently-named columns and parsed numeric measures. Use when joining HCPCS metadata to utilization facts or when filtering by HCPCS attributes. | Use for: Look up HCPCS descriptions for codes in utilization data; Filter HCPCS codes by effective/termination date or coverage flag; Aggregate utilization by HCPCS metadata fields (asc_group, statute)

views.name: icd10_procedures_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pcs_code AS pcs_code,
  is_header_code AS is_header_code,
  short_description AS short_description,
  long_description AS long_description,
  order_number AS order_number
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_procedures_2019`
grain: pcs_code  -- one row per ICD-10-PCS code or header

params.description: Reference dimension of ICD-10-PCS procedure codes and headers: returns one row per PCS code or header with descriptions and an ordering value.
params.when_to_use: Look up human-readable short and long descriptions for a given ICD-10-PCS code (pcs_code). | Filter or label facts by whether a code is a header row (is_header_code). | Sort or canonicalize lists of PCS codes using provided order_number. | Compose with utilization, charge, or provider facts to annotate procedure-level measures with code descriptions without changing measure cardinality. | Build aggregated reports by joining procedure facts to this dimension to get readable labels and ordering.
params.output_schema: pcs_code: ICD-10-PCS code or header identifier — derived from bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_procedures_2019.pcs_code | is_header_code: boolean-like flag indicating whether the row represents a header/section rather than an actual procedure code — derived from bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_procedures_2019.is_header_code | short_description: short human-readable description for the PCS code — derived from bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_procedures_2019.short_description | long_description: longer human-readable description for the PCS code — derived from bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_procedures_2019.long_description | order_number: numeric ordering value useful for sorting codes in their canonical sequence — derived from bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_procedures_2019.order_number
params.metric: This view contains no derived numeric measures or aggregates. All output columns are direct projections of base table columns: | pcs_code = bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_procedures_2019.pcs_code | is_header_code = bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_procedures_2019.is_header_code | short_description = bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_procedures_2019.short_description | long_description = bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_procedures_2019.long_description | order_number = bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_procedures_2019.order_number
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact tables or views that record procedures (example key: pcs_code) using an equality join on pcs_code — safe because icd10_procedures_dim has one row per pcs_code so it will not multiply fact rows' measures. | Safe join example: JOIN icd10_procedures_dim d ON fact.pcs_code = d.pcs_code — this annotates each fact row with code text without duplicating fact-level measures. | Do NOT join without care to one-to-many tables that expand codes (for example a hypothetical mapping table that maps a single pcs_code to many categories) unless you re-aggregate afterwards, because such joins will duplicate measures from downstream fact tables. | Do NOT assume is_header_code implies exclusivity in other joins; if you join to a table that contains both header and non-header entries linked by a different key, verify the join key is pcs_code to preserve 1:1 mapping. | When composing into aggregator queries: if you join this dimension to a pre-aggregated fact (e.g., person_event_counts_by_domain or inpatient/outpatient charge aggregates), join on pcs_code and then aggregate only columns from the fact (sums, counts). Do not sum or aggregate any columns from this dimension — they are descriptive. | This view is dimension-only (no measures). It is safe to join to sibling normalized views such as inpatient_charges_yearly_provider_drg or outpatient_charges_yearly_provider_apc on pcs_code provided those sibling views use pcs_code as a key at their grain; confirm that the sibling view's grain is per-procedure code or includes pcs_code distinctly to avoid accidental many-to-one multiplication.

views.description: Clean ICD-10-PCS procedures dimension: one row per pcs_code with descriptions and header flag preserved. Use for mapping procedure codes to human-readable text or filtering out header codes. | Use for: Join PCS descriptions to procedure-level utilization; Filter out header codes (is_header_code = TRUE) when counting valid procedures; Search procedures by keywords in descriptions

views.name: icd10_diagnoses_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cm_code AS cm_code,
  is_header_code AS is_header_code,
  short_description AS short_description,
  long_description AS long_description,
  order_number AS order_number
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_diagnoses_2019`
grain: cm_code  -- one row per ICD-10 diagnosis code or header

params.description: Reference dimension of ICD-10 diagnosis codes (one row per ICD-10 code or header) providing code, header flag, short and long descriptions, and ordering.
params.when_to_use: Look up human-readable descriptions for ICD-10 diagnosis codes when labeling or filtering clinical/claims data. | Join to claims, diagnosis, or encounter facts to translate stored diagnosis codes to descriptions. | Compose into analytics that aggregate counts or costs by diagnosis code or by header code (after appropriate joins to fact tables). | Build hierarchies or ordered lists of diagnosis codes for UI pickers, reports, or grouping by order_number.
params.output_schema: cm_code: ICD-10 diagnosis code string — derived directly from bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_diagnoses_2019.cm_code | is_header_code: boolean/indicator that the row is a header (not a leaf diagnosis) — derived from bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_diagnoses_2019.is_header_code | short_description: short human-readable label for the code — derived from bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_diagnoses_2019.short_description | long_description: longer human-readable description — derived from bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_diagnoses_2019.long_description | order_number: numeric ordering value used to sort codes or headers — derived from bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_diagnoses_2019.order_number
params.metric: This view has no derived numeric metrics. All output columns are direct pass-through columns from the source table (no aggregate expressions).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact or aggregate tables on cm_code using equality (this view is one-row-per-cm_code so joining it to a fact table that has many rows per cm_code will not duplicate the dimension's rows — it enriches each fact row). Example: JOIN icd10_diagnoses_dim d ON fact.cm_code = d.cm_code — safe because icd10_diagnoses_dim is unique per cm_code. | You may safely join this view to provider, hospital, or other dimension tables (e.g., hospitals_dim_normalized) when enriching those tables with diagnosis descriptions, because icd10_diagnoses_dim is one-row-per-code and will not multiply rows from those other one-row-per-key dimensions as long as joins remain on single-valued keys. | Do NOT join this view to another one-to-many table or view without re-aggregation on the many side if you intend to preserve aggregated measures from that many-side table. For example, do not join icd10_diagnoses_dim directly to person_event_counts_by_domain or inpatient/outpatient charges facts and then sum across diagnosis rows without grouping by the fact's primary key — those joins will duplicate fact measures if the fact side has multiple rows per cm_code. Instead, either: | - aggregate the fact table first to one row per cm_code (e.g., SUM(measure) GROUP BY cm_code) and then join to this view; or | - join the dimension to the fact and then compute aggregates grouping by the fact primary key and the dimension fields as needed. | Do NOT assume ordering is preserved across joins; use order_number from this view only for presentation/sorting after you have applied any aggregation required. | Examples of safe compositions: | - Enrich claims facts: SELECT f.*, d.short_description FROM claims_fact f LEFT JOIN icd10_diagnoses_dim d ON f.cm_code = d.cm_code | - Aggregate measures by diagnosis: WITH agg AS (SELECT cm_code, COUNT(1) AS cnt FROM claims_fact GROUP BY cm_code) SELECT a.cm_code, d.short_description, a.cnt FROM agg a LEFT JOIN icd10_diagnoses_dim d ON a.cm_code = d.cm_code | Examples of unsafe direct compositions without re-aggregation: | - Joining icd10_diagnoses_dim to a multi-row-per-person events table (person_event_counts_by_domain) and then summing event counts without first collapsing the events per person per cm_code, because the many-side will multiply rows and over-count measures.

views.description: Canonical ICD-10 diagnosis dimension: one row per cm_code with descriptions and header flag preserved. Use for mapping diagnosis codes to descriptions or filtering header rows. | Use for: Map diagnosis codes to descriptions for reporting; Exclude header diagnosis rows when counting codes; Search diagnoses by description text

views.name: physicians_top_hcpcs_rank_per_provider_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  npi,
  hcpcs_code,
  SAFE_CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64) AS year,
  line_srvc_cnt,
  bene_unique_cnt,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY npi, SAFE_CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64) ORDER BY SAFE_CAST(line_srvc_cnt AS FLOAT64) DESC) AS rank_by_line_srvc_cnt
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.physicians_and_other_supplier_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2012' AND '2015'
grain: npi, hcpcs_code, year  -- one row per provider-HCPCS-year with rank within provider-year

params.description: For each provider (NPI), HCPCS procedure code, and year (2012–2015), gives the provider-year rank of that HCPCS by number of submitted service lines, plus the raw service-line and unique-beneficiary counts — useful to see a provider's top billed HCPCS codes each year and compare their relative volume within that provider-year.
params.when_to_use: Find a provider's top HCPCS codes in a specific year (e.g., "what are the top 10 HCPCS codes for NPI X in 2014 by line_srvc_cnt?") | Compare the relative importance of specific HCPCS codes within a provider-year (e.g., "is HCPCS Y among the top 3 procedures for provider Z in 2013?") | Compose provider-year level analyses that need a HCPCS-level rank so downstream SQL can filter to top-N codes per provider-year before aggregating | Build dashboards that show per-provider yearly HCPCS rank and volume (line counts and unique beneficiaries) and then join to HCPCS metadata for labels
params.output_schema: npi: provider National Provider Identifier (derived from physicians_and_other_supplier_* . npi) | hcpcs_code: HCPCS procedure code (derived from physicians_and_other_supplier_* . hcpcs_code) | year: integer year parsed from the table suffix (SAFE_CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64)) representing the claims year; source: table suffix in physicians_and_other_supplier_* | line_srvc_cnt: number of submitted service lines for that provider-hcpcs-year (derived from physicians_and_other_supplier_* . line_srvc_cnt) | bene_unique_cnt: number of unique beneficiaries for that provider-hcpcs-year (derived from physicians_and_other_supplier_* . bene_unique_cnt) | rank_by_line_srvc_cnt: integer rank of this HCPCS within the same provider and year, ordered by line_srvc_cnt descending (computed as RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY npi, year ORDER BY CAST(line_srvc_cnt AS FLOAT64) DESC))
params.metric: line_srvc_cnt = base column physicians_and_other_supplier_*.line_srvc_cnt (no aggregation in this view; reported as present in the source row) | bene_unique_cnt = base column physicians_and_other_supplier_*.bene_unique_cnt (no aggregation in this view) | rank_by_line_srvc_cnt = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY npi, SAFE_CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64) ORDER BY SAFE_CAST(line_srvc_cnt AS FLOAT64) DESC)  (rank of line_srvc_cnt within each npi-year partition)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to HCPCS dimension(s) such as hcpcs_canonical on hcpcs_code (e.g., ON physicians_top_hcpcs_rank_per_provider_year.hcpcs_code = hcpcs_canonical.hcpcs_code) — safe because this view is one row per (npi, hcpcs_code, year); joining to a one-row-per-hcpcs dimension will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to year or provider-level normalized views that are one-row-per-key, for example providers_ranked_by_total_medicare_payment_within_year on (npi, year) — safe only if that sibling view is one-row-per-(npi,year). Confirm the sibling view's grain before joining to avoid duplication. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views that expand hcpcs_code or npi into multiple rows (for example a free-text claims detail table or any view that records multiple events per (npi,hcpcs_code,year)) without first aggregating them back to (npi, hcpcs_code, year). Such joins would multiply line_srvc_cnt and bene_unique_cnt and invalidate rank semantics. | do NOT join to tables that are one-to-many on npi within a year (e.g., provider locations or specialty lists that have multiple rows per npi-year) unless you first reduce the right-side to one row per (npi, year) or use aggregation on the results to avoid duplicating this view's measures. | when composing aggregations on top of this view (for example: sum line_srvc_cnt across a set of HCPCS or compute average rank per provider), treat line_srvc_cnt and bene_unique_cnt as measures at the (npi,hcpcs_code,year) grain and re-aggregate explicitly (SUM, AVG, COUNT_DISTINCT as appropriate). | if you need to join to physicians_utilization_hcpcs_joined or other JOIN sibling views, verify their grain. Joining to another view that is also one-row-per-(npi,hcpcs_code,year) is safe; joining to a view at a different, more granular grain is not safe without pre-aggregation.

views.description: Per-provider-per-year HCPCS ranking by line service count. Exposes rank so callers can filter to top-K procedures per provider per year. Use for top-K analyses of which HCPCS each provider billed most frequently. | Use for: Select top-N HCPCS per provider in a given year by service count; Compare top billed procedures across providers or states; Examine beneficiary counts for top procedures

views.name: physicians_utilization_hcpcs_joined
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.npi AS npi,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS year,
  p.hcpcs_code AS hcpcs_code,
  p.hcpcs_description AS hcpcs_description_fact,
  h.SHORT_DESCRIPTION AS hcpcs_short_description_dim,
  h.LONG_DESCRIPTION AS hcpcs_long_description_dim,
  p.line_srvc_cnt AS line_srvc_cnt,
  p.bene_unique_cnt AS bene_unique_cnt,
  p.average_medicare_payment_amt AS avg_medicare_payment_amt,
  p.average_medicare_allowed_amt AS avg_medicare_allowed_amt,
  p.nppes_provider_state AS provider_state,
  p.place_of_service AS place_of_service,
  h.COV AS coverage_indicator,
  h.MCM1 AS mcm1
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.physicians_and_other_supplier_*` AS p
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.hcpcs` AS h
  ON p.hcpcs_code = h.HCPC
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2012' AND '2015'
grain: npi, hcpcs_code, year  -- denormalized provider-HCPCS-year row

params.description: Denormalized provider × HCPCS × year rows combining Medicare physician/supplier utilization metrics with HCPCS code descriptions and coverage flags for 2012–2015.
params.when_to_use: Get counts and average payment metrics for a specific provider (NPI), HCPCS code, and year. | Compare utilization or average payments for a given HCPCS across providers or years. | Filter provider-HCPCS rows by place_of_service or provider_state while retaining HCPCS description and coverage metadata. | Build aggregated summaries (e.g., total line_srvc_cnt by provider or HCPCS, average payment weighted by counts) using this view as the grain source.
params.output_schema: npi: provider National Provider Identifier (from p.npi). | year: calendar year string from the source table suffix (from _TABLE_SUFFIX — values '2012'..'2015'). | hcpcs_code: HCPCS/CPT code as reported in the physicians_and_other_supplier_* table (from p.hcpcs_code). | hcpcs_description_fact: HCPCS short/label text as present in the physicians_and_other_supplier_* source (from p.hcpcs_description). | hcpcs_short_description_dim: HCPCS short description from the HCPCS dimension table (from h.SHORT_DESCRIPTION). | hcpcs_long_description_dim: HCPCS long description from the HCPCS dimension table (from h.LONG_DESCRIPTION). | line_srvc_cnt: number of service lines (count of service occurrences) for this provider–HCPCS–year row (from p.line_srvc_cnt). | bene_unique_cnt: number of unique beneficiaries receiving this HCPCS from this provider in the year (from p.bene_unique_cnt). | avg_medicare_payment_amt: average Medicare payment amount for this provider–HCPCS–year row (from p.average_medicare_payment_amt). | avg_medicare_allowed_amt: average Medicare-allowed amount for this provider–HCPCS–year row (from p.average_medicare_allowed_amt). | provider_state: provider's NPPES state code (from p.nppes_provider_state). | place_of_service: place of service code as reported in the physicians_and_other_supplier_* table (from p.place_of_service). | coverage_indicator: coverage indicator/COV flag from HCPCS dimension (from h.COV). | mcm1: MCM1 flag from HCPCS dimension (from h.MCM1).
params.grounded_columns: bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.physicians_and_other_supplier_*.npi | bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.physicians_and_other_supplier_*.hcpcs_code | bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.physicians_and_other_supplier_*.hcpcs_description | bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.physicians_and_other_supplier_*.line_srvc_cnt | bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.physicians_and_other_supplier_*.bene_unique_cnt | bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.physicians_and_other_supplier_*.average_medicare_payment_amt | bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.physicians_and_other_supplier_*.average_medicare_allowed_amt | bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.physicians_and_other_supplier_*.nppes_provider_state | bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.physicians_and_other_supplier_*.place_of_service | bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.physicians_and_other_supplier_*.<table_suffix> (exposed as year via _TABLE_SUFFIX) | bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.hcpcs.HCPC | bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.hcpcs.SHORT_DESCRIPTION | bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.hcpcs.LONG_DESCRIPTION | bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.hcpcs.COV | bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.hcpcs.MCM1
params.metric: line_srvc_cnt = direct fact column p.line_srvc_cnt (count of service lines for this provider–HCPCS–year row; NOT an aggregate in the view — preserved per-row metric). | bene_unique_cnt = direct fact column p.bene_unique_cnt (unique beneficiaries for this provider–HCPCS–year row). | avg_medicare_payment_amt = direct metric column p.average_medicare_payment_amt (per-row average payment as reported; to derive totals multiply by line_srvc_cnt or bene_unique_cnt as appropriate and re-aggregate). | avg_medicare_allowed_amt = direct metric column p.average_medicare_allowed_amt (per-row average allowed amount; re-weight when aggregating).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to HCPCS canonical/dimension tables (e.g., hcpcs_canonical or hcpcs_canonical-like on hcpcs_code = HCPC or code) — safe because this view already left-joined the hcpcs dimension producing at most one matching HCPCS row per hcpcs_code; joining to a canonical HCPCS dimension keyed 1:1 on code will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE: join to provider/hospital-level single-row-per-NPI dims (e.g., hospitals_dim_normalized if mapped by provider NPI or providers_ranked_by_total_medicare_payment_within_year aggregated by NPI+year) on npi (+ year when the sibling view is year-scoped) — safe when the target is one-row-per-npi or one-row-per-npi-year so this view's metrics remain unduplicated. | DO NOT join without re-aggregation to one-to-many tables/views keyed only by npi (or hcpcs_code) that contain multiple rows per npi×year×hcpcs (for example, any raw claim-level or multi-row provider-event tables) because such joins will multiply line_srvc_cnt and bene_unique_cnt. If you must join to a one-to-many table, either: |   - aggregate that table to the npi×hcpcs_code×year grain (SUM/COUNT/AVG as appropriate) before joining, or |   - join on additional keys that make the relationship 1:1 (and validate uniqueness), or | When composing aggregates from this view: |   - to compute totals (sum of services) safely: SUM(line_srvc_cnt) over the desired grouping. |   - to compute weighted averages across rows: weighted_avg_payment = SUM(avg_medicare_payment_amt * line_srvc_cnt) / NULLIF(SUM(line_srvc_cnt),0). Do not AVG(avg_medicare_payment_amt) unweighted when you want overall average payment per service. | Example safe joins: |   - Join to physicians_top_hcpcs_rank_per_provider_year on (npi, year) — safe if that sibling view is 1 row per (npi, year, hcpcs_code) or per (npi, year) depending on join keys used and duplication risk is understood. |   - Join to hcpcs_canonical on hcpcs_code = code (one-to-one HCPCS dimension) — safe because hcpcs dimension is canonical 1:1. | Example unsafe joins (without pre-aggregation): |   - Do NOT join directly to person_event_counts_by_domain or observations_latest_per_person_concept_rank without aggregating them to the same npi×hcpcs_code×year grain; they are multi-row event aggregates and could multiply counts. | Rationale: this view's measures (line_srvc_cnt, bene_unique_cnt) are stored at the npi×hcpcs_code×year grain (denormalized provider-HCPCS-year row). Any join that introduces multiple rows per that same grain will multiply those measures unless the added side is first reduced to 1 row per grain or the join is constrained to a guaranteed 1:1 match.

views.description: Denormalized view joining physician utilization facts to HCPCS canonical dimension. Preserves provider, hcpcs, year and exposes both utilization measures and HCPCS metadata for filtering and grouping. | Use for: Assess payment differences by HCPCS attributes; Filter utilization by HCPCS coverage or metadata; Rank HCPCS within providers using enriched metadata

views.name: inpatient_charges_yearly_provider_drg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_id AS provider_id,
  provider_name AS provider_name,
  provider_street_address AS provider_street_address,
  provider_city AS provider_city,
  provider_state AS provider_state,
  provider_zipcode AS provider_zipcode,
  drg_definition AS drg_definition,

params.composition: Cardinality-safe joins (do NOT duplicate measures): |  - Join to provider/physician dimension views on referring_npi (e.g., physicians_top_hcpcs_rank_per_provider_year or hospitals_dim_normalized if keyed by NPI) — safe because this view is one row per (referring_npi, year). Joining a 1:1 provider dimension keyed by referring_npi (and optionally year) will not duplicate supplier_medicare_payment_amount or number_of_suppliers. |  - Join to a provider name/metadata dimension keyed by referring_npi (for attributes like name, specialty, address) is safe because those dimensions should be one row per NPI; ensure the dimension is deduplicated to 1 row per NPI before joining. |  - Join across year to other yearly-per-provider views that are also one row per (referring_npi, year) (for example, other *_per_provider_year RANK/NORM views) on (referring_npi, year) — safe because both sides are at the same grain. |  | Joins that will multiply/duplicate measures (avoid unless you re-aggregate): |  - Do NOT directly join to any one-to-many detail table (for example: claims-level, events, or supplier-level rows) keyed only by referring_npi without first aggregating that detail to the (referring_npi, year) grain. Doing so will multiply supplier_medicare_payment_amount and number_of_suppliers and produce incorrect totals. |  - Do NOT join to suppliers list or supplier-level tables that have multiple supplier rows per referring_npi and year without aggregating suppliers to a single row per referring_npi-year first, because number_of_suppliers and supplier_medicare_payment_amount would be duplicated or need re-aggregation. |  - Do NOT join to person_event_counts_by_domain, observations_latest_per_person_concept_rank, or other person- or event-level views that are many-per-provider unless aggregated to provider-year first. |  | Guidance for correct composition: |  - If you must combine with a one-to-many view, first aggregate the many-side to (referring_npi, year) producing compatible measures (e.g., SUM(payment) AS supplier_medicare_payment_amount, COUNT(DISTINCT supplier_id) AS number_of_suppliers) and then JOIN on (referring_npi, year). |  - When joining to sibling RANK views that compute ranks over different measures, prefer joining on both referring_npi and year to preserve the per-year partitioning semantics. |  - This view's rank_by_medicare_payment is computed per year using supplier_medicare_payment_amount values present in the source tables; if you filter rows (for example, to a subset of providers) after joining, ranks will not automatically recompute — recompute rank if you need ranking restricted to the filtered set.

views.name: person_event_counts_by_domain
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.person_id,
  COALESCE(obs.observation_count, 0) AS observation_count,
  COALESCE(drug.drug_exposure_count, 0) AS drug_exposure_count,
  COALESCE(cond.condition_occurrence_count, 0) AS condition_occurrence_count,
  COALESCE(proc.procedure_occurrence_count, 0) AS procedure_occurrence_count,
  COALESCE(dev.device_exposure_count, 0) AS device_exposure_count,
  (COALESCE(obs.observation_count, 0)
   + COALESCE(drug.drug_exposure_count, 0)
   + COALESCE(cond.condition_occurrence_count, 0)
   + COALESCE(proc.procedure_occurrence_count, 0)
   + COALESCE(dev.device_exposure_count, 0)) AS total_event_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person` AS p
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT person_id, COUNT(1) AS observation_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.observation`
  GROUP BY person_id
) AS obs
ON p.person_id = obs.person_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT person_id, COUNT(1) AS drug_exposure_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure`
  GROUP BY person_id
) AS drug
ON p.person_id = drug.person_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT person_id, COUNT(1) AS condition_occurrence_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.condition_occurrence`
  GROUP BY person_id
) AS cond
ON p.person_id = cond.person_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT person_id, COUNT(1) AS procedure_occurrence_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.procedure_occurrence`
  GROUP BY person_id
) AS proc
ON p.person_id = proc.person_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT person_id, COUNT(1) AS device_exposure_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.device_exposure`
  GROUP BY person_id
) AS dev
ON p.person_id = dev.person_id

params.description: Per-person counts of events broken down by OMOP domain (observation, drug_exposure, condition_occurrence, procedure_occurrence, device_exposure) plus their person-level total.

params.output_schema: person_id: unique identifier for the person — sourced from bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person.person_id | observation_count: integer count of observation records for the person — derived from COUNT(1) over bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.observation.person_id (aliased observation_count) | drug_exposure_count: integer count of drug_exposure records for the person — derived from COUNT(1) over bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure.person_id (aliased drug_exposure_count) | condition_occurrence_count: integer count of condition_occurrence records for the person — derived from COUNT(1) over bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.condition_occurrence.person_id (aliased condition_occurrence_count) | procedure_occurrence_count: integer count of procedure_occurrence records for the person — derived from COUNT(1) over bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.procedure_occurrence.person_id (aliased procedure_occurrence_count) | device_exposure_count: integer count of device_exposure records for the person — derived from COUNT(1) over bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.device_exposure.person_id (aliased device_exposure_count) | total_event_count: integer sum of the five domain counts for the person — expression summing the COALESCE(...) values for observation_count, drug_exposure_count, condition_occurrence_count, procedure_occurrence_count, device_exposure_count

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to person-level dimension or attribute views/tables on person_id (for example, any normalized persons dimension or the base person table) — safe because this view already has exactly one row per person_id, so a 1:1 or many-to-1 join does not duplicate counts. | cardinality-SAFE: aggregate this view up (GROUP BY) to higher grains (e.g., by demographic groups, by provider if you first join persons to a provider_id and then GROUP BY provider) — safe because you are summing per-person counts rather than joining raw event tables. | UNSAFE: do NOT directly inner-join or left-join this view to any event-level or other one-to-many tables (for example, joining to drug_exposure, condition_occurrence, procedure_occurrence, observation, device_exposure, or any view that expands person into multiple rows per event) without first aggregating the many-side to person_id. Doing so will multiply the event counts (measure duplication) because this view's counts are already aggregated per person. | UNSAFE: do NOT join to provider-level or visit-level fact tables that contain multiple rows per person_id (or multiple rows per person per time-window) unless you aggregate that table to one row per person_id (or to the exact same grain) before joining — otherwise counts will be inflated. | SAFE pattern examples: | - To compute count of persons per cohort who have >=1 drug_exposure: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM person_event_counts_by_domain WHERE drug_exposure_count >= 1; | - To get total drug exposures per provider: first aggregate drug_exposure by provider_id and person_id or by provider_id alone (depending on desired grain), or join person_event_counts_by_domain to a person->provider mapping that is 1:1 and then SUM(drug_exposure_count) grouped by provider_id. | JOIN guidance referencing available sibling views: | - You can join to observations_latest_per_person_concept_rank (RANK) on person_id safely if that sibling view is 1:1 per person (confirm its grain). If that sibling view is multi-row per person, aggregate it first. | - Do NOT join this view directly to physicians_utilization_hcpcs_joined (JOIN) or inpatient_charges_yearly_provider_drg (NORM) unless those are pre-aggregated to one row per person_id; they are likely provider/fact-level and will duplicate counts. | - Safe to join to persons/person dimension (bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person) on person_id — this view was built from that table and is 1 row per person.

params.description: One-row-per-observation with a stable rank of each observation per person+observation_concept_id (latest first).
params.when_to_use: Find the latest (or top-N) observation rows for each person and observation_concept_id | Filter to the most-recent observation per person+concept before joining to other tables (e.g., keep rank_within_person_concept = 1) | Compute person-level summaries or cohorts that rely on the latest observation value for each concept | Serve as a base when you need the most recent observation timestamp/value per person+concept and avoid scanning the full observation table each time
params.output_schema: observation_id: the primary key of the observation row as stored in `observation.observation_id` | person_id: the person identifier from `observation.person_id` — the person who had the observation | observation_concept_id: the OMOP concept id for the observation from `observation.observation_concept_id` | observation_date: the date of the observation from `observation.observation_date` | observation_datetime: the timestamp of the observation from `observation.observation_datetime` (may be NULL) | observation_type_concept_id: the type of observation from `observation.observation_type_concept_id` | value_as_number: numeric value for the observation from `observation.value_as_number` | value_as_string: textual value for the observation from `observation.value_as_string` | value_as_concept_id: coded value for the observation from `observation.value_as_concept_id` | qualifier_concept_id: qualifier concept id from `observation.qualifier_concept_id` | unit_concept_id: unit concept id from `observation.unit_concept_id` | provider_id: provider identifier from `observation.provider_id` | visit_occurrence_id: visit occurrence id from `observation.visit_occurrence_id` | visit_detail_id: visit detail id from `observation.visit_detail_id` | observation_source_value: source value string from `observation.observation_source_value` | observation_source_concept_id: source concept id from `observation.observation_source_concept_id` | rank_within_person_concept: 1-based row number per (person_id, observation_concept_id) ordered by most-recent observation (uses observation_datetime if present else observation_date), ties broken by highest observation_id; computed as ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY person_id, observation_concept_id ORDER BY COALESCE(observation_datetime, CAST(observation_date AS DATETIME)) DESC, observation_id DESC)
params.metric: rank_within_person_concept = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY person_id, observation_concept_id ORDER BY COALESCE(observation_datetime, CAST(observation_date AS DATETIME)) DESC, observation_id DESC) | note: there are no aggregated numeric metrics in this view (value_as_number is a passthrough column, not an aggregate)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to person-level dimension or table on person_id — safe because this view remains one row per observation; if you restrict to rank_within_person_concept = 1 first, the join becomes one-row-per-person-per-concept and will not duplicate those 'latest' rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a concept/dimension table on observation_concept_id or observation_source_concept_id — safe because concept tables are one-row-per-concept (one-to-one), so joining will not duplicate rows from this view. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables (for example an events table keyed to observation_id that contains multiple child rows) without re-aggregation or additional keys — joining to a child table on observation_id will multiply this view's rows and therefore duplicate any implicit measures (for example counting rows or summing value_as_number). If you need aggregated child data, pre-aggregate the child by observation_id before joining. | do NOT join this view to another view that is one-row-per-(person,concept) and then assume measures are independent unless you verify keys — joining two multi-row-per-person resources on person_id only will create cross-products unless you further restrict or aggregate. To preserve cardinality, either (a) restrict to rank_within_person_concept = 1 (making it one-latest-per-person-per-concept) before joining and join on (person_id, observation_concept_id) to another one-row-per-(person,concept) resource, or (b) aggregate this view to the desired grain (e.g., one row per person) before joining to one-row-per-person tables. | example safe patterns: |   - To get the latest observation value per person+concept and attach concept names: SELECT v.*, c.concept_name FROM observations_latest_per_person_concept_rank v JOIN concept_dim c ON v.observation_concept_id = c.concept_id WHERE v.rank_within_person_concept = 1; |   - To compute per-person counts of latest concepts: use WHERE rank_within_person_concept = 1 and then aggregate by person_id; this prevents double-counting multiple historical observations for the same concept. | example unsafe pattern: |   - Joining observations_latest_per_person_concept_rank (without filtering rank) to a medication_events table on person_id — this produces a many-to-many expansion (all observations × all medications for the person).

views.description: Latest observation per person+observation_concept_id with a rank column. Useful to pick the most recent measurement or to keep top-K recent observations per person-concept. | Use for: Retrieve latest lab values per person for cohort definitions; Compute deltas between most recent and previous observations using rank/filter rank<=2 downstream; Filter to most recent observation per person-concept for model features
